references.text: Herod hears about Jesus and believes it is John the Baptist who has risen from the dead – the parallel account in Matthew.
Mark's parallel account where Herod hears about Jesus and thinks that John, whom he himself had beheaded, has risen from the dead.
Mark tells of the actual beheading of John the Baptist, which Herod refers to when he says 'John I beheaded'.
Matthew's account of the beheading of John the Baptist, which Herod alludes to in his statement.

The immediate context where it is reported what people said about Jesus – that he was John risen from the dead, or Elijah, or one of the ancient prophets – which forms the background for Herod's confusion.
Herod's desire to see Jesus is fulfilled during the trial when Pilate sends Jesus to Herod, and Herod had long wanted to see him and hoped to witness a sign.
The Pharisees warn Jesus that Herod wants to kill him, showing Herod's continued interest in and concern about Jesus.
Luke tells that Herod imprisoned John the Baptist, which is the background story for the beheading Herod mentions here.
